definitions.explanation: Can refer to literal gatekeepers or figurative guardians.

examples.japanese: {門番|もんばん}に{名前|なまえ}を{告|つ}げた。
examples.english: I gave my name to the gatekeeper.

examples.japanese: {城|しろ}の{門番|もんばん}が{通行|つうこう}を{許可|きょか}した。
あの{編集者|へんしゅうしゃ}は{出版|しゅっぱん}{業界|ぎょうかい}の{門番|もんばん}のような{存在|そんざい}だ。
examples.english: That editor is like a gatekeeper of the publishing industry.

notes:
Composed of {門|もん} (gate) + {番|ばん} (guard, watch). Refers to a person who guards or controls access at a gate. Also used figuratively in modern Japanese to describe anyone who controls access to an organization, industry, or resource.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {城|しろ}の{門番|もんばん}: castle gatekeeper
- {門番|もんばん}を{務|つと}める: to serve as gatekeeper
- {門番|もんばん}のような{役割|やくわり}: a gatekeeper-like role

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {守衛|しゅえい}: security guard (modern, at buildings or facilities)
- {番人|ばんにん}: watchman, guard (broader usage)
- {警備員|けいびいん}: security guard (professional, modern)
- ゲートキーパー: gatekeeper (loanword, often used in business contexts)
